From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>

Subject: QBR readiness: product + eng roadmap status and delivery risks

Team —

Attaching the latest artifacts ahead of the QBR prep slot on Tuesday. Key asks below:

Attachments: qbr-risk-matrix-v2.xlsx, product-timeline-v3.pptx

Summary (TL;DR):
- Product and core infra are on the same delivery cadence but we have 3 cross-team risks that could push our GA window: infra capacity (KV cache scaling), model quantization regressions, and 3rd-party feature parity for embeddings.
- Acme (pilot customer) expects a firm launch commitment in the QBR; procurement will raise SLA/penalty questions if we miss the target.

Action items before Monday EOD:
1) @Laura — confirm which features in the timeline are "must ship" for Q1 vs Q2. Mark them in the slide deck.
2) @Vivek — is there executive appetite to pre-approve a small credit/contingency fund if we need to accelerate infra? (I put a placeholder in RED-5421).
3) @Priyom — triage the quantization regression tests and estimate time to remediation for the top two failing models.
4) @Stephanie — coordinate an internal canary plan for Acme; we need rollback criteria and a brief customer note.

Proposed triage call: Monday 11:00 PT (30m). I'll share the screen and run through the risk matrix. Please review the matrix and add owners inline.

Regards,
Michael
Michael Grant
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-02-15T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: QBR readiness: product + eng roadmap status and delivery risks

Thanks Michael — reviewed the matrix and the timeline. A few notes inline:

- Must-ships for Q1: API gating, Live KV cache fallback, and Embedding parity (search rerank prototype). I've updated slide 2 to flag those as "Q1 must".
- Soft-ships (Q2): UX polish items, advanced admin controls.

Risks:
- INF-1 (KV cache scaling) — blocked by a scheduler bug; Eng estimates ~2 weeks to patch + 3 days of soak for our testbench. Priyom, can you confirm resource availability?
- MQT-2 (quantization regression) — failing for the new 4-bit path on longer sequences; putting a conservative fallback in the runtime is low-risk and buys us time.

Customer impact: Acme will be tolerant of a staged rollout if we provide a clear canary plan and guaranteed fallback to hosted model with slightly higher latency.

I've attached an updated timeline (product-timeline-v3.pptx) with colors for Q1/Q2.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Engineering, Product Delivery
Redwood Inference

Looping in my perspective before the Monday triage:

- On credit/contingency: I'm open to a small pre-approved credit to Acme (up to 5% of ARR for the pilot) to keep them on the program if we need a short delay. Sales should scope how that affects renewal economics.
- On infra acceleration: I'm comfortable approving a Dedicated pool reservation for a 4-week sprint if engineering can show (1) a measurable latency improvement and (2) a firm rollback plan. Laura — please prepare the measurement deck (P95/P99 before vs after).

Escalation suggestion: If INF-1 remains unresolved at the end of the triage, we'll escalate to Ops leadership and propose the dedicated reserve + temporary throttling on non-critical workloads. That gives us a blunt but controllable mitigation.

I also want a concrete customer communication draft for Acme that sets expectations while signalling our mitigations. Stephanie — can you prepare a 3-bullet note that we can send post-triage?

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR readiness: product + eng roadmap status and delivery risks — decisions and owners

Short summary and decisions from today's triage (for the record):

1) INF-1 (KV cache scaling) — Owner: Priyom Das. Mitigation: reserve a Dedicated pool for 4 weeks; Eng gets 2 additional SRE FTEs for patch + soak. Contingency: temporary throttling on non-critical workloads.
2) MQT-2 (quantization regression) — Owner: Laura Bennett. Mitigation: runtime conservative fallback for affected models; add regression guard in CI and a plan to re-enable 4-bit path after soak.
3) EMB-3 (embedding parity) — Owner: Stephanie Nguyen. Mitigation: staged canary with Acme; fallback to hosted embedding endpoint documented in customer note.

Actions (owners + due dates):
- Priyom: commit patch plan and timeline by 2026-02-23T18:00:00-08:00; create RED-5533 and link to RED-5421.
- Laura: measurement deck (P95/P99) and canary rollout playbook by 2026-02-24T12:00:00-08:00.
- Stephanie: customer note draft and internal rollback criteria by 2026-02-22T10:00:00-08:00.
- Finance/Sales: Sales to provide impact of a 5% pilot credit by 2026-02-21. HubSpot deal: 549812.

I uploaded an updated risk matrix and the final timeline to the QBR folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqQBRPrep.

Next steps: if owners hit blockers, escalate to Vivek + Ops. I'll take point on Exec communication if we need to formalize a revised commitment to Acme.

Thanks all — we'll present this at the QBR working session on Tuesday.

Michael
Michael Grant
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
